item.title: Following the Silk Road to a Festive Season in the Maldives
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
This festive season, the Maldives becomes a meeting point of cultures as Vakkaru Maldives draws inspiration from the historic Silk Road for nearly four weeks of celebrations, from December 13, 2026, through January 9, 2027. Set within the UNESCO Biosphere Reserve of Baa Atoll, the program brings together international cuisine, live entertainment, wellness experiences, and activities for families against the backdrop of the Indian Ocean. Highlights include a Christmas Eve gala dinner beneath the stars on Vakku Beach, sunset wine tastings on a private sandbank, and a Silk Road-inspired New Year’s Eve celebration featuring global flavors and fireworks over the water. At Merana Spa, Japanese holistic practitioner Yoko Kawaguchi leads a special residency, adding a restorative dimension to the festivities. The celebrations continue into January with Orthodox Christmas traditions, extending the holiday season beyond the usual calendar and inviting guests to experience the Maldives through a distinctly international lens.

The Curated Take

The historic Silk Road was more than a route for trade; it was a passage through which ideas, traditions, and cultures met and evolved. Bringing that spirit to a Maldivian island creates an intriguing approach to the festive season, where culinary discovery and cultural influences become part of the celebration. For travelers seeking a luxury holiday escape with a sense of connection beyond the shoreline, Vakkaru’s program offers a reminder that some of the most rewarding journeys happen when different traditions share the same table.

item.title: A Classic New York Christmas, from Holiday Carols to the Times Square Ball Drop
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
New York City takes on a special kind of magic during the holidays, when festive music, seasonal treats, and beloved traditions transform Midtown into a winter wonderland. At InterContinental New York Barclay, the season brings classic New York celebrations together with thoughtful experiences for families and travelers of all ages. Thanksgiving and Christmas dining at The Parlour sets the scene for seasonal gatherings, while the annual Barclay Express: Cookies & Cocoa invites families to decorate cookies and sip hot chocolate. Throughout the week of December 14, holiday choirs fill the lobby with music, and a postcard station offers guests the chance to send greetings to loved ones or Santa, whose replies may arrive at their guestrooms by way of the hotel’s elves. Younger guests can retreat to the Petit Chalet, a cozy A-frame hideaway stocked with blankets, pillows, and classic board games. The celebrations culminate on New Year’s Eve, when guests can welcome the year ahead at The Parlour while watching the iconic Times Square Ball Drop.

The Curated Take

Few cities make the holidays feel as cinematic as New York, where familiar rituals take on an extra sparkle against the energy of Midtown. From handwritten holiday greetings and carols in the lobby to watching the Times Square Ball Drop without stepping into the winter crowds, the Barclay’s seasonal experiences offer a more intimate way to enjoy the city’s festive spirit. For families and couples planning a New York holiday escape, it is an invitation to experience the season through small traditions, shared moments, and the unmistakable atmosphere of the city at its most celebratory.

item.title: A Season of Holiday Traditions in Plymouth, Michigan
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
From Thanksgiving gatherings to Christmas magic and New Year’s Eve celebrations, Plymouth, Michigan, offers a festive-season escape filled with family traditions and elegant occasions. At Saint John’s Resort, the holidays begin with a Thanksgiving feast featuring traditional favorites and interactive dessert stations, followed the next day by a Christmas tree lighting in the Monarch Courtyard, where twinkling lights, live carolers, hot cocoa, and fireside gatherings welcome the season. Families can add a little enchantment to their December stay with a holiday sleepover experience that includes an in-room visit from one of Santa’s helpers, a bedtime story, breakfast, and a special meeting with Santa. As the year draws to a close, The Wine Grotto hosts a New Year’s Eve celebration with an elaborate buffet, live music, and an evening designed for welcoming 2027. Together, these seasonal experiences make the resort an appealing destination for a festive family getaway or a celebratory holiday stay in the Detroit area.

The Curated Take

The holidays often become most memorable through the rituals shared along the way, from the first lights on a Christmas tree to the excitement of a child awaiting a visit from Santa. In Plymouth, Saint John’s Resort brings these moments together with celebrations for different generations, balancing family-friendly traditions with sophisticated dining and a spirited New Year’s gathering. For travelers seeking a holiday escape closer to home, it offers an opportunity to turn familiar seasonal customs into a special occasion without an elaborate journey.

item.title: Winter Wildlife Encounters in Jackson Hole, Wyoming
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Winter transforms Jackson Hole, Wyoming, into a remarkable setting for wildlife watching, as snow-covered landscapes make animal coats and tracks stand out against the white terrain. Sunrise and sunset safaris with local naturalist guides offer opportunities to observe elk, moose, bighorn sheep, and other wildlife while taking in views of the Teton Range. Snowshoeing excursions provide a closer connection to the region’s ecology, while dog sledding brings a more exhilarating way to explore the valley. At the National Elk Refuge, seasonal sleigh rides offer a memorable perspective on one of the area’s defining wildlife spectacles, as thousands of elk gather across protected winter habitat. For travelers planning a winter nature escape, Jackson Hole combines extraordinary wildlife encounters with access to Grand Teton National Park and the surrounding mountain landscape, while the Wyoming Inn offers a convenient base for exploring the region’s outdoor attractions.

The Curated Take

There is something extraordinary about encountering wildlife on its own terms, with a vast winter landscape creating the conditions to observe rather than simply pass through. In Jackson Hole, tracks etched into fresh snow and herds gathered across the National Elk Refuge reveal a different dimension of the American West. Guided by local experts who interpret the connections between animals and their environment, these experiences offer more than a sighting: they invite travelers to understand the rhythms of a wild landscape in winter.

item.title: Skating and Fireside Fondue in Austria’s Winter Alps
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
In Leogang, Austria, winter days unfold against the dramatic peaks of the Leoganger Steinberge, where outdoor ice skating and the warmth of traditional alpine dining set the scene for a seasonal escape. This winter, Forsthofgut Nature Hotel introduces a new outdoor ice rink with mountain views, alongside a new slopeside home for Restaurant 1617. After time on the ice, guests can warm up with mulled wine, hot chocolate, and roasted chestnuts before settling into wood-paneled dining rooms for Austrian specialties and cheese, meat, or chocolate fondue beside a tiled stove or open fireplace. During the Advent season, additional festive touches, including homemade Christmas cookies and a seasonal spa treatment, bring together alpine traditions, comforting flavors, and restorative wellness. For travelers seeking a winter escape in the Austrian Alps, Leogang offers a balance of outdoor pleasures and fireside indulgence.

The Curated Take

Some of winter’s most memorable pleasures are wonderfully uncomplicated: the crisp air of the mountains, the exhilaration of time on the ice, and the warmth of a shared meal as the evening settles in. In Leogang, alpine scenery provides the backdrop for a seasonal experience grounded in Austrian culinary traditions and the comforts of a fireside gathering. It is an invitation to embrace winter at its most elemental, with fresh mountain air by day and fondue, warm drinks, and unhurried evenings after dark.

item.title: A Christmas in the English Countryside: Dorset’s Winter Charms
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Across 100 acres of Dorset farmland, Christmas offers an opportunity to trade the rush of the season for the pleasures of the English countryside. At Louma Country Hotel, festive stays unfold in a collection of restored farm buildings and shepherd huts, with seasonal dining and thoughtful touches setting the tone for a country Christmas. Families can fill their days with treasure hunts, movie nights, and gingerbread decorating, while adults find time for wellness at the Wellness Barn, alongside wine and cocktail experiences. Beyond the estate, Dorset’s festive markets and seasonal events bring a sense of local tradition, while fossil discovery walks along the Jurassic Coast offer a distinctly regional way to explore the winter landscape. Together, countryside comforts, family activities, and coastal discovery make Dorset an appealing setting for a festive escape in southern England.

The Curated Take

There is a particular pleasure in a country Christmas that leaves room for both tradition and discovery. In Dorset, days can move from gingerbread decorating and fireside-style country comforts to the remarkable geology of the Jurassic Coast, where ancient fossils tell a story far older than the holiday season. For travelers seeking a slower, more grounded festive escape, this corner of England offers a reminder that the richest seasonal experiences often come from the landscape itself, and the freedom to enjoy it at an unhurried pace.

item.title: A Storybook Christmas in Austria’s Snowbound Alps
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
In Oberlech, a car-free alpine village in Austria’s Arlberg region, Christmas unfolds amid snow-covered mountain scenery and traditions that bring generations together. On Christmas Eve, carols led by the Lucian family and the Mozarteum Salzburg String Quartet fill the lobby of Burg Hotel Lech, followed by Santa Claus arriving with presents for younger guests as the quartet accompanies Christmas dinner. Throughout Advent, a calendar of daily surprises adds to the anticipation, while New Year’s Eve brings a party and live DJ to welcome 2027. With its village setting, musical traditions, and celebrations designed around family, Oberlech offers a distinctly Austrian take on a white Christmas, pairing the magic of the winter Alps with the warmth of a holiday spent together.

The Curated Take

A memorable Christmas escape is often less about spectacle than the traditions that make a place feel special. In Oberlech, live classical music, familiar carols, and the anticipation of Santa’s arrival create a festive atmosphere rooted in the pleasures of gathering together. Set in a car-free alpine village, the experience offers travelers a chance to embrace the quieter magic of an Austrian white Christmas, where snow-covered surroundings provide the setting and shared rituals become the lasting memories.

item.title: Christmas and New Year Beneath the Palms in the Maldives
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
In the Maldives, the festive season unfolds beneath swaying palms, with ocean views and island experiences offering a tropical alternative to traditional winter celebrations. From December 22, 2026, through January 7, 2027, Baros Maldives brings guests together for a series of Christmas and New Year gatherings, beginning with a cocktail reception at The Lighthouse and continuing with a Christmas Eve gala dinner at Lime. As the year draws to a close, another reception sets the stage for a New Year’s Eve gala dinner and countdown. Beyond the formal celebrations, an island Christmas market and hands-on experiences, including a festive cookie workshop, a cooking class exploring Maldivian seafood, and cocktail-making sessions, invite guests to share in the season through food, craftsmanship, and convivial island life. For those seeking a luxury festive escape in the Indian Ocean, the celebrations offer a way to mark the holidays in a setting shaped by warm waters and the unhurried rhythm of island living.

The Curated Take

The appeal of a festive island escape lies not simply in exchanging snow for sand, but in discovering how familiar traditions take on a new character in a different setting. In the Maldives, shared meals, a Christmas market, and hands-on culinary experiences create opportunities for connection beyond the usual holiday spectacle. It is a reminder that the most memorable celebrations often come from the rituals shared along the way, whether gathered around a festive table or welcoming a new year beneath the palms.

item.title: Christmas by Long-Tail Boat: Festive Traditions on Thailand’s Andaman Coast
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
On Thailand’s Andaman Coast, Christmas takes on a distinctly tropical character, where turquoise waters and starlit beaches replace the familiar winter landscape. In Krabi, the festive season begins at Phulay Bay with Santa arriving by traditional Thai long-tail boat, followed by carols, fire dancing, and a festive buffet and market fair beneath the night sky. As the celebrations turn toward New Year’s Eve, sunset cocktails and a gala dinner featuring Thai cultural performances give way to a beachside DJ countdown and fireworks over the ocean. Set within a secluded retreat of villas and pavilions, the experience brings together the warmth of familiar holiday traditions and the cultural character of southern Thailand, offering a different perspective on a luxury Christmas escape in Southeast Asia.

The Curated Take

For travelers ready to trade frosted windows for tropical horizons, Thailand offers a festive season shaped by a different rhythm. Here, long-tail boats, traditional performances, and celebrations beneath the stars bring a sense of place to Christmas and New Year’s, while the Andaman Sea provides a striking backdrop. It is a reminder that holiday traditions need not be left behind when traveling far from home; they can become something entirely new when encountered through another culture.
